{{nihongo|'''Mino Agatanushi Shrine'''|御野縣主神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Yao, Osaka|Q490872|qid=Q490872}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, and its former shrine rank was village shrine. {{nihongo|'''Mino Agatanushi Shrine'''|御野縣主神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

== History / Overview ==
It is the tutelary shrine of former Kaminoshima Village (Kaminoshima area of Yao City) in old {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}}{{ill|Kawachi district|Q11553458|qid=Q11553458|lt=Kawachi District}}. It enshrines the ancestral deity of powerful families that once ruled this area: the Mino no Muraji and Mino Agatanushi line.

The date of foundation is unknown, but because the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} records two seats of Mino Agatanushi Shrine in {{ill|Wakae district|Q11616589|qid=Q11616589}}, Kawachi Province, it is considered to have existed before the Heian period. In Meiji 5 (1872), it was ranked as {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

The west side of the precinct is a small rise, the former embankment trace of {{ill|Tamagushi River|Q11572360|qid=Q11572360|lt=Tamagushi River}} (old {{ill|Yamato River|Q9001527|qid=Q9001527}}), once flowing on the west side. It is said to survive only here today. It is designated as protected woodland by Yao City and is a valuable historic site. South of the precinct is Mino Agata Pond.

== Festivals ==
* July 2 - Summer festival
* Second Saturday/Sunday of October - Autumn festival (futon-daiko procession)

== Other ==
* {{ill|2022|Q49625|qid=Q49625}}, appeared on TV Tokyo’s {{ill|Emergency SOS! We Drained the Pond!|Q30938102|qid=Q30938102}}

== Shikibe-no-Miya ==
[[ファイル:Shikibe-Minoagatanushi Jinja01.JPG|thumb|right|200px|Shikibe Mino Agatanushi Shrine]]
Slightly south of the main shrine, by Higashiyamamotochō 5-chōme Park, there is another seat called “Shikibe Mino Agatanushi Shrine” (Shikibe-no-Miya). It has only a shrine building on a small plot. This place was at the edge of a settlement in former {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takayasu District}}{{ill|Higashiyamamotochō|Q11526717|qid=Q11526717|lt=Manganji Village}}; in the mid-Edo period, when the village split in a water-rights dispute and the Shikibe settlement moved south to Manganji Village, a divided spirit was invited there.
